title: One Fibonacci parastichy pair necessarily entails all the lower pairs

fields.label: Label
fields.value: One Fibonacci parastichy pair necessarily entails all the lower pairs

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Following Tait, if a single genetic spiral exists and one pair of parastichy numbers from the series 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13… is present, all the lower pairs of the series are necessarily present in the same system.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: F_{n+1} = F_n + F_{n-1} (1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, \dots); pair (F_n, F_{n+1}) present \Rightarrow all lower pairs present

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XIV: On Leaf-Arrangement, or Phyllotaxis

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: These are the very series which we have found to be common, or normal; and so far as our investigation has yet gone, it has proved to us that, if one of these exists, it entails, _ipso facto_, the presence of the rest.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XIV, “On Leaf-Arrangement, or Phyllotaxis”; topic “Tait's explanation of the numbers”. Scope: spiral phyllotactic systems with a single genetic spiral

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: F_{n+1} = F_n + F_{n-1} (1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, \dots); pair (F_n, F_{n+1}) present \Rightarrow all lower pairs present

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch14-07: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.81

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The necessity statement is a crisp combinatorial prediction once the genetic spiral is indexed. Existing images can supply many tests, and model-based enumeration avoids relying only on visual prominence.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reconstruct the indexed genetic spiral from high-resolution organ maps, enumerate every parastichy family, and test whether observation of a higher Fibonacci pair always co-occurs with all lower pairs under one prespecified visibility-independent definition. A single valid counterexample refutes necessity; universal co-occurrence in broad data supports it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Implicit mathematical parastichies must be distinguished from visually conspicuous ones.

Occlusion can hide lower-order connections.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim is Tait's geometric result that one Fibonacci contact pair on a single spiral brings the lower pairs with it. Once a specimen is regular enough to have a divergence and one pair, the other pairs are the same set of lattice lines counted another way. Data can illustrate the arithmetic, and they cannot confirm or refute it without changing the subject to whether real plants are regular spirals.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Given a single regular genetic spiral, the presence of one Fibonacci parastichy pair already fixes the lattice, and the lower pairs are alternate contact directions in that same lattice. Counting them on a cone restates the geometry; it does not distinguish the theorem from a rival empirical hypothesis.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Visible versus latent pairs depend on which diagonals the eye picks out, which is a drawing convention.

A system that violated the entailment would have failed the premise of one regular genetic spiral, not supplied an independent biological outcome.
